claims.text: The untreated starting material is a W–Cu composite with interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The untreated composite is produced by SPS at 900 °C, 50 MPa, and 10⁻³ Torr without an interfacial coating.
A Ni coating approximately 100 nm thick is deposited on all W surfaces before sintering.
The Ni coating forms a graded Ni–W–Cu interphase during SPS.
The interphase is a Ni–W–Cu intermetallic phase at the W/Cu boundary.
The Ni interlayer promotes wetting at the W/Cu interface.
The Ni interlayer promotes interdiffusion at the W/Cu interface.
Ni-assisted interdiffusion forms a graded solid solution.
The graded interphase lowers W/Cu interfacial energy.
Lower interfacial energy suppresses interfacial void nucleation under thermal stress.
The Ni-containing interphase suppresses interfacial void nucleation under irradiation.
The Ni-containing interphase enhances thermal contact conductance.
After exposure to 800 °C and 1 dpa neutron irradiation in He, the Ni-coated composite will have more than 10% higher thermal conductivity than the untreated composite.
After irradiation, the Ni-coated composite will have more than 20% lower interfacial void density than the untreated composite.
The proposed effect applies to SPS processing at 850–950 °C, 30–70 MPa, and hold times of approximately 30 minutes.
The proposed effect applies in He coolant at service temperatures up to 900 °C and irradiation doses up to 1 dpa.
The magnitude of the performance gain may vary with Ni thickness.
The magnitude of the performance gain may vary with the exact sintering parameters.

contradictions.description: The mediator is identified as a Ni–W–Cu intermetallic interphase, whereas the mechanism identifies the formed graded phase as a solid solution; these are materially distinct phase descriptions and are not reconciled.

The hypothesis predicts more than a 10% thermal-conductivity increase, but the falsification rule accepts an increase of only 5% as sufficient, so outcomes between 5% and 10% fail the stated prediction without satisfying the stated falsification condition.
